chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who doubted and did not know whether he had prostrated one prostration or two. He said: 'He should prostrate until he is certain.'
If he did not know whether he had prostrated one or two, he said: 'Then let him prostrate another one.'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they doubt the number of prostrations in their prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *Istishab* (presumption of continuity) in resolving doubts during prayer, specifically addressing the scenario of uncertainty between one and two prostrations. It prescribes performing an additional prostration (*Sajdat al-Shakk*) to rectify the doubt, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ensuring the validity of obligatory acts through tangible corrective actions rather than mere speculation.
